ap_microeconomics-m01.stem: In a competitive labor market, a union convinces some workers to retire early, which reduces the number of workers willing to work at every wage, while at the same time higher demand for the product raises the marginal revenue product of labor. Which statement describes the effect on the equilibrium wage and employment?

options.text: Employment falls and the wage is indeterminate, because the shifts push the wage in opposite directions.
options.why: Both shifts raise the wage, so the wage is determinate; employment is the indeterminate variable.

options.text: The wage rises and employment falls, because labor supply is the only curve that shifts.
options.why: Labor demand also shifts right, which offsets the fall in employment.

options.text: The wage rises, but the change in employment is indeterminate, because labor supply shifts left and labor demand shifts right.
options.why: A leftward supply shift and a rightward demand shift both raise the wage; employment falls with the supply shift and rises with the demand shift, so its change depends on the sizes.

options.text: The wage falls and employment is indeterminate, because fewer workers lower the wage.
options.why: Fewer workers raise, not lower, the wage when supply shifts left.

options.text: Employment rises and the wage rises, because demand for the product increased.
options.why: Ignores the supply decrease; a smaller labor force reduces the quantity of labor supplied at each wage.

facts: variant=In a competitive labor market, a union c

ap_microeconomics-m01.stem: Two things happen at once in a competitive labor market for warehouse workers: a new scanning technology raises each worker's marginal product, and a wave of new residents increases the number of people willing to work at every wage. Which statement describes the effect on the equilibrium wage and employment?

options.text: Employment is indeterminate, but the wage rises, because demand and supply shift in opposite directions.
options.why: Both curves shift right, so employment rises with certainty and the wage is the indeterminate variable.

options.text: The wage rises and employment rises, because greater productivity always raises wages.
options.why: Ignores the supply shift; more workers put downward pressure on the wage.

options.text: The wage falls and employment falls, because more workers compete for the same jobs.
options.why: Ignores the demand shift and mislabels employment; both shifts raise employment.

options.text: Neither the wage nor employment changes, because the two shifts cancel each other out.
options.why: The shifts offset only in the wage in special cases; both increase the quantity of labor employed.

options.text: Employment rises, but the change in the wage is indeterminate, because labor demand shifts right and labor supply shifts right at the same time.
options.why: Higher productivity shifts labor demand right (wage up, employment up) and more workers shifts labor supply right (wage down, employment up); employment rises for sure, the wage depends on which shift is larger.

ap_microeconomics-m02.stem: A restaurant uses cooks and ovens together, and the two inputs are complements in production. The price of ovens falls. Holding the wage constant, which statement correctly describes the effect on the restaurant's demand for cooks?

options.text: The quantity of cooks demanded decreases along the labor demand curve, because ovens cost less.
options.why: A change in another input's price shifts the whole curve; it is not a movement along the curve.

options.text: The demand for cooks decreases, because lower costs of ovens reduce the restaurant's output.
options.why: Lower input costs raise the profit-maximizing output.

options.text: The demand for cooks increases, because cheaper ovens raise the marginal product of cooks and the restaurant expands output.
options.why: When inputs are complements, a cheaper partner input raises the productivity of labor and the scale of output, so labor demand shifts right.

options.text: The demand for cooks is unaffected, because the wage has not changed.
options.why: A change in the price of a complementary input shifts labor demand even if the wage is unchanged.

options.text: The demand for cooks decreases, because the restaurant substitutes ovens for cooks.
options.why: Treats complements as substitutes.

facts: variant=A restaurant uses cooks and ovens togeth

ap_microeconomics-m02.stem: A restaurant can make meals with either cooks or automated kitchen machines, and the two are substitutes in production. The price of the automated machines falls sharply. Holding the wage constant, which statement correctly describes the effect on the restaurant's demand for cooks?

options.text: The demand for cooks decreases by the full amount, because the output effect never matters.
options.why: Ignores the output effect that partly offsets the substitution effect.

options.text: The demand for cooks increases, because the restaurant is producing more meals.
options.why: Reports only the output effect and ignores the substitution of machines for cooks.

options.text: The demand for cooks is unaffected, because labor demand depends only on the wage.
options.why: Labor demand also depends on the prices of other inputs and on the product price.

options.text: The quantity of cooks demanded increases along the same labor demand curve, because machines are cheaper.
options.why: A change in another input's price shifts the labor demand curve rather than moving along it.

options.text: The restaurant substitutes machines for cooks, which tends to decrease the demand for cooks, though the larger output it can now afford works in the opposite direction.
options.why: A cheaper substitute input lowers demand for labor through the substitution effect, partly offset by an output effect when lower costs raise production.

facts: variant=A restaurant can make meals with either

ap_microeconomics-f01.title: Total variable cost of producing ceramic mugs per day for one firm in a perfectly competitive market where the price is $19 per unit. The firm's total fixed cost is $21 per day

stimulus.description: Total variable cost of producing ceramic mugs per day for one firm in a perfectly competitive market where the price is $19 per unit. The firm's total fixed cost is $21 per day.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the quantity that maximizes the firm's profit in the short run.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Produce while the marginal cost of the next unit is at most the price of $19; the marginal cost of unit 3 is $18 and of unit 4 is $22, so the firm produces 3 units.

required_elements: Compares the price with marginal cost from the changes in total variable cost and chooses the last unit whose marginal cost does not exceed the price (the answer is correct)
alt_solutions: price equals marginal cost
produce until marginal cost would exceed the price
common_errors: picks the quantity with the lowest average variable cost
produces the largest quantity in the table
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the firm's economic profit or loss at that quantity.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Total revenue = $19 x 3 = $57; total cost = $21 + $42 = $63; the firm has a loss of $6.

required_elements: Subtracts total fixed cost plus total variable cost from total revenue to get a loss (the answer is correct)
alt_solutions: revenue minus total cost
total revenue less fixed and variable cost
common_errors: leaves out the fixed cost
reports total revenue as the profit
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Should the firm produce in the short run or shut down? Identify your choice.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. It should keep producing in the short run, because total revenue exceeds total variable cost (the price is above average variable cost), so the firm loses less than the fixed cost it would lose by shutting down.

required_elements: States that the firm should keep producing rather than shut down
alt_solutions: operate in the short run
stay open
common_errors: says the firm should shut down because it has a loss
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain why your answer to part (C) is correct for the short run even though the firm has an economic loss.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. The fixed cost of $21 must be paid whether the firm operates or not, so shutting down would lose $21; by operating, revenue covers all the variable cost with $15 left over to cover part of the fixed cost, so the loss is only $6.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains with revenue covering variable cost and fixed cost being sunk
required_elements: States that revenue covers variable cost, with something left over toward the fixed cost, so operating loses less than shutting down, where the whole fixed cost is lost
alt_solutions: the fixed cost is sunk in the short run
price is above average variable cost
common_errors: says the firm earns a profit
says the fixed cost can be avoided by shutting down in the short run
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: If the price stays at this level, describe what will happen to the number of firms in this industry in the long run and explain why.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Firms exit the industry, because in the long run all costs are avoidable and a firm earning a loss would leave; exit reduces market supply and raises the price until firms earn zero economic profit.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains exit until zero economic profit
required_elements: States that firms leave the industry in the long run because of economic losses, which raises the price toward the level where economic profit is zero
alt_solutions: market supply decreases and the price rises
fixed costs are avoidable in the long run
common_errors: says new firms enter the industry
says the number of firms stays the same because firms earn normal profit
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

The fixed cost of $37 must be paid whether the firm operates or not, so shutting down would lose $37; by operating, revenue covers all the variable cost with $25 left over to cover part of the fixed cost, so the loss is only $12.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains with revenue covering variable cost and fixed cost being sunk
required_elements: States that revenue covers variable cost, with something left over toward the fixed cost, so operating loses less than shutting down, where the whole fixed cost is lost
alt_solutions: the fixed cost is sunk in the short run
price is above average variable cost
common_errors: says the firm earns a profit
says the fixed cost can be avoided by shutting down in the short run
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: If the price stays at this level, describe what will happen to the number of firms in this industry in the long run and explain why.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Firms exit the industry, because in the long run all costs are avoidable and a firm earning a loss would leave; exit reduces market supply and raises the price until firms earn zero economic profit.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains exit until zero economic profit
required_elements: States that firms leave the industry in the long run because of economic losses, which raises the price toward the level where economic profit is zero
alt_solutions: market supply decreases and the price rises
fixed costs are avoidable in the long run
common_errors: says new firms enter the industry
says the number of firms stays the same because firms earn normal profit
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

blueprint.concept: Profit-maximizing quantity from marginal cost, economic loss, the shutdown rule, and long-run exit
student_thinking: Find marginal cost from total variable cost
Compare revenue with total cost and with variable cost
Reason about sunk fixed cost and long-run exit

key_conditions.condition: Competitive output market with the price and the fixed cost stated in the table title

verification.independent_path: argmax of total profit across quantities vs last unit with marginal cost at most the price

parts.label: A
accepted_answers: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Produce while the marginal cost of the next unit is at most the price of $21; the marginal cost of unit 5 is $20 and of unit 6 is $22, so the firm produces 5 units.

elements: Compares the price with marginal cost from the changes in total variable cost and chooses the last unit whose marginal cost does not exceed the price (the answer is correct)

parts.label: B
accepted_answers: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Total revenue = $21 x 5 = $105; total cost = $37 + $80 = $117; the firm has a loss of $12.

elements: Subtracts total fixed cost plus total variable cost from total revenue to get a loss (the answer is correct)

parts.label: C
accepted_answers: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. It should keep producing in the short run, because total revenue exceeds total variable cost (the price is above average variable cost), so the firm loses less than the fixed cost it would lose by shutting down.

elements: States that the firm should keep producing rather than shut down
